toegepas.voor: lê baie lande teen die see
toegepas.na: lê baie lande aan die see
toegepas.rede_vinder: A country lies 'aan die see' in idiomatic Afrikaans; 'teen die see' can read as 'against the sea'.
toegepas.fout: 'lande lê teen die see' is not the fixed Afrikaans expression for a country on the coast
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'aan die see' is the natural fixed expression for a place on the coast, and the location stays the same, so the meaning does not move.

toegepas.blok: Zanzibar: eilande wat aan 'n land behoort
toegepas.rede_vinder: The bare noun 'See' as subject is unnatural; the definite article is needed.
toegepas.fout: bare 'See' as the subject reads unnaturally
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Die see skei die eilande' is what a fluent writer would write, and the meaning is unchanged.

toegepas.blok: Zanzibar: eilande wat aan 'n land behoort
toegepas.voor: maar nie altyd een is nie
toegepas.na: maar dit nie altyd is nie
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'een is nie' is a wooden reference; 'dit nie altyd is nie' is the natural form and gives the clause after the comma its own subject.
toegepas.fout: 'nie altyd een is nie' copies the English 'isn't always one'
toegepas.rede_keurder: Afrikaans normally uses 'dit' to refer back to a predicate ('maar dit nie altyd is nie'), and the claim stays exactly the same.

vlae.teks: Party lande word aan alle kante deur ander lande omring en het geen kus nie.
vlae.rede: Not a language fault, so not changed: the body says 'deur ander lande' (plural), while the decided definition of landgeslote uses 'deur land' because Lesotho is surrounded by one country, which the next sentence says. A person may want the body to match.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: in die Indiese Oseaan oos van Mosambiek
laat_vaar_vorige.na: in die Indiese Oseaan, oos van Mosambiek
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A comma separates the two place phrases so 'oos van Mosambiek' is not read as part of the ocean's name or location.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The phrase reads naturally without a comma, AWS does not require one here, and either reading places Madagascar east of Mozambique, so the change is lateral.
